title: U.S. House · Montana's 2nd District
area: Eastern Montana, including Billings and Great Falls.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Troy Downing (R) did not face a primary challenger in 2026, winning renomination unopposed.

summary.text: Troy Downing is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Montana's 2nd Congressional District. He is a former Montana state auditor and insurance commissioner who serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the Small Business Committee.

background.text: Raised in Indio, California; studied computer science at New York University.

Co-founded WebCal, an internet-based calendar system later incorporated into Yahoo in 1998, and was CEO of AC Self Storage Solutions; also operated a commercial real estate development firm and created a commercial insurance company.
Was previously a member of the Montana Land Board as a former statewide official.

priorities.text: Supports making the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act permanent and has introduced legislation aimed at expanding rural small businesses' access to capital.

Supports an "all-of-the-above" energy approach that emphasizes coal, oil and gas production in Montana, including legislation to keep the Bull Mountains coal mine open and to support Signal Peak's mining operations.

positions.summary: Calls fossil fuels an abundant, cost-efficient energy source, supports coal and oil and gas development, and opposes federal rules such as the MATS rule and a fracking ban.
In a March 2026 questionnaire, said the President may act swiftly with limited engagement while Congress reviews, but that sustained combat requires formal congressional authorization.
positions.quote: If operations extend into sustained combat, Congress must provide formal authorization or determine the appropriate course forward.

positions.summary: Says he has supported policies that reduce regulatory barriers to building new housing.
positions.quote: I've also supported policies that expand access to capital and reduce regulatory barriers that make it harder to build new housing.

record.text: Sits on the House Financial Services Committee and the Small Business Committee (Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Workforce Development; and Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.
Introduced the Federal Insurance Office Elimination Act to eliminate the Federal Insurance Office.

Introduced the Expanding Access to Capital for Rural Job Creators Act, which would require the SEC's Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation to identify capital-access challenges facing rural small businesses.

candidates.name: Brian Miller
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary with 55.5% of the vote over Sam Lux and Jonathan Windy Boy (who unofficially withdrew).

summary.text: Brian Miller is the Democratic nominee for Montana's 2nd Congressional District.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 questionnaire, said only Congress has the power to declare war and that he would put Congress back in charge of any use of military force against a foreign nation.
positions.quote: If I’m elected to Congress, I will make sure that we put Congress back in charge of any use of military force against any foreign nation, no matter how slight.

positions.summary: Names restoring Medicaid funding and the ACA subsidies among his first priorities and calls for repealing and replacing the One Big Beautiful Bill's Medicaid cuts.
positions.quote: Restore Medicaid funding and the ACA subsidies.

positions.summary: Says the regulatory process for building houses is too slow and expensive and should be streamlined.
positions.quote: We need to streamline that process if we want to get serious about this issue.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions drawn from the Montana Free Press March 2026 candidate questionnaire; no campaign issues page was reviewed.

candidates.name: Patrick McCracken
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed after the Libertarian primary was canceled.

summary.text: Patrick McCracken is the Libertarian Party nominee for Montana's 2nd Congressional District.

priorities.text: Says he would write a bill to codify the Ratepayer Protection Pledge on data centers, co-sponsor the American Beef Labeling Act and champion SAFE Banking.
priorities.quote: I will write the bill to codify the Ratepayer Protection Pledge. I will co-sponsor the American Beef Labeling Act. I will champion SAFE Banking from the committee Downing is sitting in.

priorities.text: Says price transparency is the first step in healthcare reform.
priorities.quote: Price transparency is the first step on a long journey.

priorities.text: Says he would require hospitals and clinics to post cash prices and let every American open a health savings account.
priorities.quote: Require hospitals and clinics to post real cash prices.

positions.summary: In an October 2026 Montana Free Press questionnaire, says he would work to pass legislation removing everyone in the country illegally under existing law.
positions.quote: As your Representative, I will work with any member of Congress to pass legislation removing everyone here illegally under existing law.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 Montana Free Press questionnaire, says the federal side of Medicaid expansion needs protecting; in October he proposed health savings accounts and catastrophic plans open to everyone.
positions.quote: Medicaid expansion is the single biggest thing keeping the lights on in rural Montana healthcare.

candidates.researchNotes: Basic-tier research from the Montana Free Press March 2026 questionnaire and October 2026 immigration and healthcare features. His campaign website has only a sign-up page. No statements found on abortion, guns, taxes, or climate.

statements.quote: Congress has always had the power to declare war and the power of the purse. They don't use either.
statements.context: In a March 2026 Montana Free Press questionnaire

candidates.name: Michael Eisenhauer

summary.text: Michael Eisenhauer is an independent candidate for Montana's 2nd Congressional District.

priorities.text: Says he will fight to defend and protect rural healthcare in Montana.
priorities.quote: I will fight hard to defend and protect rural healthcare in Montana

priorities.text: Supports restoring Medicaid and SNAP cuts with a bipartisan coalition.
priorities.quote: Work with a bipartisan coalition to restore cuts in Medicaid and SNAP assistance, without delay

priorities.text: Supports defined term limits for Members of Congress and the Senate.
priorities.quote: I support clearly defined term limits for Members of Congress and the Senate

positions.summary: On his campaign website, describes himself as pro-choice and says the federal government should address differences in abortion access between states.
positions.quote: I am, and will remain firmly Pro-Choice.

positions.summary: On his campaign website, supports a 72-hour waiting period and closing the gun-show loophole, and also supports revising the National Firearms Act to exclude suppressors and short-barreled long guns from Form 1 and Form 4 submission.
positions.quote: Regulating a 72-hour wait-period between purchase and taking possession of a firearm, including gun shows

positions.summary: On his campaign website, says removing illegal immigrants convicted of serious crimes is reasonable, and that he is worried ICE is being overly aggressive; opposes deporting Dreamers.
positions.quote: It is entirely reasonable to remove illegal immigrants who have been convicted of serious crimes or violence against others.

positions.summary: On his campaign website, lists zoning changes allowing duplexes, triplexes and multi-family housing among his housing proposals.
positions.quote: Zoning changes that remove barriers to the construction of duplexes, triplexes or multi-family housing in residential areas

positions.summary: On his campaign website, says he will work to protect and increase federal funding for police and emergency services.
positions.quote: I will work to protect and increase federal funding for these vital services; I will make sure that Montana law enforcement and first responders always have the resources they need.

positions.summary: On his campaign website, says current tariffs have been excessive and hurt the economy by raising costs for consumers and businesses.
positions.quote: Tariffs will not make America rich again.

positions.summary: On his campaign website, says he does not believe a single-payer system will be workable, and says he would work with a bipartisan coalition to restore Medicaid cuts.
positions.quote: Work with a bipartisan coalition to restore cuts in Medicaid and SNAP assistance, without delay

candidates.researchNotes: Basic-tier research from his campaign website issues page and Montana Free Press October 2026 questionnaires. No statements found on rent regulation, school choice, minimum wage, or Israel aid.

statements.quote: It is not fair to cut or reduce taxes on multi-millionaires, billionaires and large multi-national corporations, while the middle-class and small businesses continue to shoulder our tax burden.
I support an "all of the above" energy policy that supports a wide range of domestic energy sources
